questions.prompt: Explain how the onboarding backend's generic validate middleware works: what it takes as arguments, which Zod call it uses and what it does on failure, where the 400 response is actually produced and with what body, what it does with the parsed value on success, and why splitting the work this way helps.

keyPoints.text: validate takes a Zod schema and a source of body, query or params (body by default).
It calls schema.parse, the throwing variant, not safeParse.
validate itself never touches res; it forwards the ZodError with next(error).
The global error middleware turns that ZodError into a 400 with err.flatten().fieldErrors.
keyPoints.quote: then turns it into a 400 with `err.flatten().fieldErrors`

keyPoints.text: On success, req[source] = parsed writes the coerced, stripped value back, so controllers see what Zod produced rather than the raw payload.
keyPoints.quote: so controllers see what Zod produced, not the raw payload.

keyPoints.text: One middleware owns validation and another owns the response shape, so you trace both to understand a failed request.
keyPoints.quote: One middleware owns validation, another owns the response shape

questions.prompt: How does the onboarding backend handle errors thrown in controllers? Explain how exceptions reach the global error handler instead of per-controller try/catch, what the handler logs, the three branches it takes (AppError, ZodError, anything else) and the response each produces, and why the production check in the last branch matters.

keyPoints.text: Controllers do not build error responses with manual try/catch; an async handler wrapper catches exceptions and forwards them to a centralized error boundary.
keyPoints.quote: we use an asynchronous handler wrapper to catch exceptions and forward them to a centralized global error boundary.

keyPoints.text: The error middleware logs the full error to the console.
keyPoints.quote: Log the full error to console for easy development and debugging

keyPoints.text: An AppError is answered with its own status code and a { success, errorCode, message, metadata } body.
A ZodError becomes a 400 with flattened field errors.
keyPoints.quote: a `ZodError` becomes a 400 with flattened field errors

keyPoints.text: Anything else becomes a 500 whose message is hidden when NODE_ENV is production.
keyPoints.quote: anything else becomes a 500 whose message is hidden behind `NODE_ENV === 'production'`

keyPoints.text: That one line separates a debuggable dev server from a leaky production one.
keyPoints.quote: that one line is the difference between a debuggable dev server and a leaky production one.

questions.prompt: The Express handler guide lists pitfalls that break the request pipeline. Explain what goes wrong when middleware forgets next(), when validation is ordered before auth, when an async controller is not wrapped, when a handler responds twice, and when internal errors are returned raw.

keyPoints.text: A middleware that never calls next() leaves the request hanging until the client times out.
keyPoints.quote: Failing to call `next()`, causing requests to hang until client timeout.

keyPoints.text: Putting validation before auth lets unauthenticated requests consume validation work.
keyPoints.quote: Placing request validation middleware *before* auth checks, allowing unauthenticated requests to consume validation cycles.

keyPoints.text: An async controller not wrapped in asyncHandler can cause unhandled process terminations on rejection.
keyPoints.quote: causing unhandled process terminations on rejection.

keyPoints.text: Calling res.json() twice in one handler triggers "Headers already sent" errors.
keyPoints.quote: Attempting to call `res.json()` twice inside the same handler

keyPoints.text: Returning raw backend exceptions or database parser statements to the client leaks internals.
keyPoints.quote: Returning raw backend exceptions or database parser statements to the client.
